title: Runtime length-cohort orchestrator & pad-minimizer for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Introduce a runtime component (Length Cohort Orchestrator) that groups concurrent requests into transient cohorts by effective token-length distribution, applies cohort-specific padding reduction, and emits kernel-affinity hints to the scheduler so we can reduce average token padding without regressing latency SLAs.
background: Current runtime uses coarse bucketing and conservative padding policies that prioritize p95 latency at the expense of token cost. As customer workloads diversify (many short prompts plus occasional long contexts) we can reduce cost substantially by grouping compatible requests more aggressively and using different prefill/decode schedules and kernels per group. Prior tickets focused on static seqlen bucketing and microbatch shaping; this ticket aims to (1) make cohorting dynamic and locality-aware, (2) integrate kernel-selection hints for attention variants, and (3) stage rollout to avoid tail latency regressions.
proposed_solution: 1) At request admission, compute an efficient length-signature: {prefix_len, continuation_prob_bucket, max_allowed_latency_tier} derived from request metadata and recent user history. 2) Maintain ephemeral cohorts (3–10ms lifetime) keyed by compressed signature; requests joining the cohort are queued for up to T_cohort ms (configurable, default 6ms). 3) For each cohort compute an optimal pad_target = percentile(len_distribution, p_pad) + cohort_margin where p_pad is tunable per tier. 4) Emit a kernel_affinity_hint with three scalar attributes: preferred_attention_impl (dense|flash|sparse), kv_cache_layout (contiguous|strided), and decode_strategy (prefill-first|interleaved). 5) Scheduler uses these hints to pick a kernel and GPU placement that minimizes per-token compute while preserving configured latency SLOs. 6) Add a lightweight cost/latency estimator to simulate expected p50/p95 impact and gate pad reduction via a rollout percentage. 7) Telemetry: cohort-level metrics (pad_saved_tokens, cohort_wait_ms, kernel_choice, p50/p95 by cohort).
implementation_tasks: Create admission path plugin that computes length-signature and assigns cohort IDs
Implement ephemeral cohort table with efficient lock-free join semantics
Pad-target calculator service with percentile sketch (T-Digest) tuned for tail robustness
Design kernel_affinity_hint schema and integrate with kernel selector API
Extend scheduler to accept hints and maintain fallback to default kernels if latency deviates
Add simulator to estimate token-cost and latency impact per configuration
Add cohort telemetry and console dashboard (cohort explorer) for rollout monitoring
Write unit/integration tests and a canary rollout plan with feature flags
milestones: M1: Prototype admission plugin + ephemeral cohort table (by 2026-03-10)
M3: Scheduler hint handling + simulator and e2e tests (by 2026-03-24)
M4: Canary rollout (10% traffic) + dashboard + safety kill-switch (by 2026-03-28)
acceptance_criteria: Reduce mean padded tokens per request by >= 18% on sampled production workloads (short+long mix)
No more than 5% relative regression in cohort-level p95 latency compared to baseline SLA for canary traffic
End-to-end integration tests cover kernel hinting and fallback (deterministic failure injection)
Telemetry surfaces cohort-level pad_saved_tokens and kernel_choice in Console within 2 minutes
Feature can be fully disabled with a single flag and roll back within 2 minutes
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cohort waiting increases tail latency. Mitigation: hard upper bound on wait (T_cohort) and per-request latency budget carry-through; track cohort_wait_ms and auto-disable pad reduction if p95 breaches.

Risk: Kernel affinity hints mis-route to suboptimal kernels on heterogeneous fleets. Mitigation: scheduler maintains historical cost/latency estimates and can fall back to default kernel; start with conservative hinting for non-critical tiers.

Risk: Sketch percentile errors lead to under-padding and decode thrash. Mitigation: use conservative cohort_margin, low-frequency sanity checks, and a simulator to validate extreme distributions before rollouts.
Risk: Increased complexity in telemetry. Mitigation: limit cohort cardinality by compression of length-signature and aggregate high-cardinality cohorts into an 'other' bucket for dashboards.
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal perf testing on staging with replayed traffic and simulator sweeps to find safe p_pad and T_cohort. Phase B: canary at 10% traffic for non-enterprise tier for 48h with strict p95/SLA alarms. Phase C: expand to 50% after 72h of stable metrics, then full rollout after two-week observation. Feature flagging with per-customer opt-out for Dedicated customers.
notes: Design review scheduled 2026-03-05: reviewers Marcus Lin, Aisha Patel, Sofia Rios.
We should avoid renormalizing kv-cache layout for small cohorts — prefer hint-only approach initially.
Look at recent production trace: 2026-02-20 short+long mix shows 26% wasted tokens due to coarse padding; this is the economic target.
Consider later extension: per-customer learned p_pad using online A/B and RL-style bandit to maximize savings under latency constraints.
